description: Core algebra concepts for high school

cards.back:
x = (−b ± √(b²−4ac)) / 2a

Use when ax² + bx + c = 0
steps: Write equation in standard form ax^2 + bx + c = 0.
Identify coefficients a, b, and c carefully with signs.
Simplify both plus and minus branches for two solutions.
cards.tip: Tip: Say 'opposite b, plus or minus, square root, over 2a' to lock the structure in memory.
hints: Identify a, b, c from ax^2 + bx + c = 0 before doing any arithmetic.
Compute b^2 - 4ac first; do not mix signs.
Plug into (-b ± sqrt(b^2-4ac))/(2a), then evaluate both plus and minus cases.
cards.example: A ball's height is modeled by h(t) = -16t^2 + 48t + 5. The quadratic formula finds when h(t)=0 to estimate when it hits the ground.

cards.front: What is the discriminant, and what does each case mean?
cards.back:
Δ = b²−4ac
• Δ > 0 → two real roots
• Δ = 0 → one real (repeated) root
• Δ < 0 → no real roots (complex)
steps: From ax^2 + bx + c = 0, calculate Δ = b^2 - 4ac.
Check sign of Δ: positive, zero, or negative.
Match sign to root count and type.
Use result to predict graph x-intercepts before solving fully.
cards.tip: Tip: Positive two, zero one, negative none (real) is the fast root-count chant.
hints: The discriminant uses only b and c along with a in b^2 - 4ac.
Focus on whether Δ is >0, =0, or <0.
Map sign to roots: two real, one repeated real, or complex pair.
cards.example: Design software checks the discriminant in trajectory equations to tell whether a path intersects a target at zero, one, or two points.

cards.back:
(a+b)(c+d) = ac + ad + bc + bd

First · Outer · Inner · Last
steps: Add results and combine like terms if possible.
cards.tip: Tip: Trace an X pattern between parentheses to avoid missing the middle products.
hints: Every term in the first parenthesis multiplies every term in the second.
Track order as First, Outer, Inner, Last.
After multiplying four products, combine like terms to finish.
cards.example: FOIL is used when expanding revenue or cost models such as (base + fee)(quantity + adjustment) in business spreadsheets.

cards.back:
a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)²
a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)²

cards.front: Slope formula given two points (x₁,y₁) and (x₂,y₂)

cards.back:
y = mx + b

m = slope, b = y-intercept

y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)

Useful when you know slope and one point

cards.front: Laws of Exponents: product, quotient, power
cards.back:
• aᵐ · aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ
• aᵐ / aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ
• (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ
• a⁰ = 1
• a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ

Split into two equations:
ax + b = c  →  x = (c−b)/a
ax + b = −c  →  x = (−c−b)/a

Remember: c must be ≥ 0

A relation where each input (x) maps to exactly one output (y).

Vertical Line Test: a graph is a function if no vertical line intersects it more than once.

cards.front: Factoring a trinomial: x² + bx + c
cards.back:
Find two numbers p, q such that:
• p · q = c
• p + q = b

Then: x² + bx + c = (x + p)(x + q)

cards.front: Systems of equations — substitution vs elimination
cards.back:
Substitution: solve one equation for a variable, substitute into the other.

Elimination: multiply equations to cancel a variable when added/subtracted.
